n: David asks the Lord to be his judge and vindicate him. He isn’t claiming to be sinless, but that he has lived with wholehearted loyalty and trusted God, so he won’t slip.

f.g: Here it means “vindicate me” or “defend my cause,” as a judge clears an innocent person.
Slip or waver, like losing one’s footing.

n: He invites God to test him thoroughly, the way metal is tested in fire, down to his deepest feelings and motives.

f.g: Literally the kidneys; in Hebrew thought, the seat of emotions and inner motives.
Test me, put me to the proof.

n: What keeps David steady is that God’s loyal love is always in front of his eyes. Keeping God’s kindness in view shapes how he walks.
David has avoided spending his time with empty, deceitful people. The company we keep shapes who we become.

f.g: Hypocrites; people who hide their true intentions.
Worthless or false people; literally “men of emptiness.”

n: He refuses to join the gatherings of evildoers. To “sit with” someone in Hebrew idiom means to share their counsel and way of life.

f.w: will not sit with the wicked

n: Washing hands was a sign of innocence and purity before worship. David pictures himself, clean, walking around the altar in procession.

f.g: Go around, encircle — likely a procession around the altar.

n: His purpose in coming to the altar is to praise God out loud and tell others about his wonderful works.
David loves the place where God’s glory dwells — the sanctuary. For Latter-day Saints this echoes a love of the temple as the house of the Lord.

f.w: the place where thine honour dwelleth
f.g: Literally “the place where your glory dwells” — the presence of God in the tabernacle.

n: He asks not to be swept away in the same fate as violent sinners when judgment comes.
These are people who plot harm and take bribes — corrupt in both their schemes and their dealings. The right hand stands for one’s actions and power.

f.g: Wicked plans, evil schemes — much stronger than today’s sense of playful trouble.

n: “But as for me” marks David’s choice: he will keep walking with integrity, while still asking God to redeem him and be merciful. Integrity and grace go together.
David now stands on level, solid ground, and he will praise the Lord among the gathered worshippers. The psalm ends in confident, public gratitude.

f.g: Level ground — safe footing, in contrast to slipping (verse 1).
